pharm: Selective inhibitor of fibroblast growth factor receptors 1 through 3 (FGFR1-3); blocks FGFR signaling to inhibit tumor growth in FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement-positive cholangiocarcinoma and FGFR1-rearranged myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms
quick: Cholangiocarcinoma: 13.5 mg once daily 14 days on / 7 days off (21-day cycle). MLN: 13.5 mg once daily continuously
Take with or without food at the same time each day
Can cause fetal harm; avoid - use effective contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after the last dose
No adjustment in mild-moderate; reduce dose in severe renal impairment
No adjustment in mild; reduce dose in severe hepatic impairment
No specific interaction; limit due to additive effects
Ophthalmic exams, serum phosphate, LFTs, pregnancy status
summary: Pemigatinib (Pemazyre) is a selective oral FGFR1-3 inhibitor indicated for previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusion or other rearrangement, and for relapsed or refractory myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms (MLN) with FGFR1 rearrangement. For cholangiocarcinoma the dose is 13.5 mg once daily for 14 consecutive days followed by 7 days off in 21-day cycles; for MLN it is 13.5 mg once daily continuously. Key risks include ocular toxicity with retinal pigment epithelial detachment (RPED), hyperphosphatemia with soft-tissue mineralization risk, stomatitis, nail and skin toxicity, and embryo-fetal toxicity. It has no boxed warning.
indications: Treatment of adults with previously treated, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusion or other rearrangement, as detected by an FDA-approved test
Treatment of adults with relapsed or refractory myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms (MLN) with FGFR1 rearrangement

dosage.d: 13.5 mg once daily for 14 consecutive days followed by 7 days off
dosage.t: 21-day cycles until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Confirm FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement with an FDA-approved test before starting

dosage.t: Continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: No scheduled off week for the MLN indication
Withhold for RPED, severe hyperphosphatemia, or other intolerable toxicity, then resume at reduced dose
Permanently discontinue if unable to tolerate 4.5 mg

admin: Take one dose by mouth once daily at about the same time each day, with or without food
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush, chew, split, or dissolve
For cholangiocarcinoma use the 14-days-on / 7-days-off schedule; for MLN take continuously with no off week
Obtain a comprehensive ophthalmologic exam including OCT before starting, every 2 months for the first 6 months, every 3 months thereafter, and urgently for any visual symptoms
If a dose is missed by 4 or more hours or vomiting occurs after a dose, skip it and take the next dose at the scheduled time
moa: Pemigatinib is a potent selective inhibitor of FGFR1, FGFR2, and FGFR3. By blocking FGFR autophosphorylation and downstream signaling through the RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK and PI3K/AKT pathways, it inhibits proliferation and survival of tumor cells driven by FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements (cholangiocarcinoma) and FGFR1 rearrangements (myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms). Hyperphosphatemia reflects on-target inhibition of FGFR-mediated renal phosphate excretion.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to pemigatinib or any excipient
relative: Pre-existing retinal disorders or risk factors for retinal pigment epithelial detachment
Hyperphosphatemia or disorders predisposing to soft-tissue mineralization
Severe renal or hepatic impairment (requires dose reduction)
Concomitant strong CYP3A inducers or proton pump inhibitors
monitor: Visual symptoms and OCT findings for retinal pigment epithelial detachment
Skin, nails, and mucosa for stomatitis and nail toxicity
Pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal findings, pemigatinib can cause fetal harm including embryofetal mortality and malformations. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of pemigatinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild to moderate renal impairment. For severe renal impairment, reduce the dose (e.g., 9 mg on the same schedule for cholangiocarcinoma); monitor closely.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild hepatic impairment. For severe hepatic impairment, reduce the dose (e.g., 9 mg on the same schedule for cholangiocarcinoma); monitor closely.

major: Strong CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - substantially reduce pemigatinib exposure; avoid concomitant use
Strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., itraconazole, clarithromycin) - significantly increase pemigatinib exposure; reduce the pemigatinib dose if coadministration cannot be avoided
Proton pump inhibitors - reduce pemigatinib solubility and exposure; avoid; if acid suppression is needed use an H2 antagonist with staggered dosing or a locally acting antacid
moderate: Moderate CYP3A inducers - may reduce pemigatinib exposure; monitor for loss of efficacy
Phosphate-increasing agents (e.g., vitamin D analogues, phosphate supplements) - worsen hyperphosphatemia; monitor phosphate
minor: H2-receptor antagonists and antacids may be used with separation if acid suppression is required
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no clinically significant food effect. Maintain a low-phosphate diet when phosphate is elevated.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol due to additive constitutional and hepatic effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum phosphate, renal function, and liver function tests; ophthalmologic exams with OCT for RPED.

common: Dry mouth, dry eye, and dry skin
serious: Retinal pigment epithelial detachment (RPED) with vision changes
emergency: Sudden vision loss, flashing lights, or visual field changes (RPED) - seek urgent ophthalmology
Signs of severe hyperphosphatemia with muscle cramps or calcinosis - seek urgent care
Severe mouth sores preventing hydration or nutrition

monitoring: Comprehensive ophthalmologic exam with OCT before starting, every 2 months for 6 months, every 3 months thereafter, and urgently for visual symptoms
Serum phosphate at baseline and periodically; initiate low-phosphate diet and phosphate-lowering therapy per thresholds
Liver function tests, renal function, and electrolytes periodically
Skin, nails, and oral mucosa for stomatitis and nail toxicity
Pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential
counsel: Take once a day at about the same time, with or without food; for bile duct cancer follow the 14-days-on / 7-days-off calendar
Report any vision changes such as blurred vision, flashing lights, or dark spots right away - you will need regular eye exams
Follow a low-phosphate diet and take phosphate-lowering medicine as prescribed when told your phosphate is high
Avoid antacid heartburn medicines called PPIs (such as omeprazole) unless your doctor advises; report mouth sores, nail changes, or rash
Use effective contraception and do not breastfeed; tell your doctor about all other medicines, especially antifungals, antibiotics, and seizure medicines
pk: FGFR inhibition begins with first doses; tumor responses develop over weeks
Median plasma Tmax approximately 1 to 2 hours after oral dosing
Steady state reached within about 1 week; cholangiocarcinoma dosing includes a 7-day off period each 21-day cycle
pearls: Selective FGFR1-3 inhibitor with two schedules: 14-on / 7-off for cholangiocarcinoma, continuous daily for FGFR1-rearranged MLN
Requires documented FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement (cholangiocarcinoma) or FGFR1 rearrangement (MLN) before starting
RPED can occur at any time - scheduled OCT surveillance plus urgent exam for any visual symptom
Hyperphosphatemia is an on-target class effect - manage early with diet and binders rather than stopping drug prematurely
CYP3A and gastric-pH sensitive: avoid strong inducers and PPIs; reduce dose with unavoidable strong CYP3A inhibitors
missed: If you miss a dose of pemigatinib by 4 or more hours, or if you vomit after taking a dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific treatment for pemigatinib overdose. Symptoms are not well defined but may reflect exaggerated adverse effects such as hyperphosphatemia, ocular toxicity, and mucocutaneous toxicity. Manage with supportive care, monitor serum phosphate, renal function, and vision, and provide ophthalmologic evaluation as indicated.
